title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay, Tax, and Super – Including the Peter Overton Salary Perspective
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and a look at the Peter Overton salary bracket. Fair Work Ombudsman rates.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52; the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours, then by 52. If you work 38 hours per week (the standard full-time week under the National Employment Standards), annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, that gives $52,261.44 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. From 1 July 2026, the casual minimum rate is $33.05 per hour. When using a calculator, never add casual loading on top of a rate that already includes it; instead, start with the base rate and apply the 25% separately.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my annual pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings at 12% of ordinary time earnings (from 1 July 2026). It is not part of your take-home pay. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a salary like Peter Overton's (well above that base), super is capped.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: A Practical Guide

Whether you’re negotiating a new role, comparing job offers, or simply curious about your yearly earnings, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. The standard approach is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees, the benchmark is a 38-hour week, as set by the National Employment Standards. This article walks you through the conversion, explains tax and Medicare, and looks at how superannuation fits in – including a glance at the top tax bracket that a high-profile salary such as Peter Overton’s would occupy.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

If you work 38 hours per week, the formula simplifies to:

**Annual = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,261.44 per year.

If you’re paid fortnightly, your gross fortnight is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. At the minimum wage, that’s $2,009.80 per fortnight.

### Award Rates and Casual Loading

Many employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, updated from 1 July 2026 with a 4.75% increase. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that means $33.05 per hour for casuals. When using [the timesheet](/), always enter the base hourly rate and tick the casual loading checkbox – never type a rate that already includes the loading.

### Tax and Medicare: What You Keep

Once you have your annual gross figure, the next step is estimating your take-home pay. Australia uses a progressive tax system for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on the next bracket up to $45,000
- 30% on income up to $135,000
- 37% on income up to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

Let’s apply this to a few examples.

**Example 1: Minimum wage full-time**
Annual gross: $52,261.44
Tax: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, then 30% on $7,261.44 = $2,178.43. Total tax ≈ $6,198.43. Medicare levy (2%) = $1,045.23. Net after tax and Medicare ≈ $45,017.78.

**Example 2: Average full-time earnings**
According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings in May 2026 were $2,083.70 per week. That’s an annual equivalent of $108,352.40. Tax on that: $0 on $18,200, 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, 30% on $63,352.40 = $19,005.72. Total tax ≈ $23,025.72. Medicare levy (2%) = $2,167.05. Net ≈ $83,159.63.

**Example 3: A high salary like Peter Overton’s**
While we don’t have a precise figure for the Peter Overton salary, a well-known television journalist would likely earn well above the top tax threshold of $190,000. For such a salary, the marginal rate is 45% plus the 2% Medicare levy, meaning nearly half of each additional dollar goes to tax. The conversion from hourly to annual remains the same formula, but the tax impact is substantial. You can explore different scenarios using our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it’s an additional benefit. For a salary at the Peter Overton level, the super cap means the employer contributes a maximum of $32,499.60 per year (12% of $270,830), even if the actual salary is higher.

When you see an annual salary figure, remember that super is extra. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect the calculation.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay times two. For the minimum wage, that’s $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, the fortnightly net is roughly $1,731.45. Using the [reference tables](/data) on this site, you can look up common hourly rates and see the corresponding annual, monthly, and fortnightly figures.

### Important Caveats

The annual figure here is an estimate. It assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always consult a tax professional for your personal situation.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, along with an estimate of tax and Medicare. It’s a quick way to see how a change in hours or rate affects your bottom line.

### Summary

Converting hourly to annual is simple: hourly × hours per week × 52. For a 38-hour week, that’s hourly × 1,976. The National Minimum Wage gives $52,261.44 per year. Award rates may be higher, and casual loading adds 25%. Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay, especially at higher incomes like the Peter Overton salary bracket. Super is an extra 12% paid on top. Use the tools on this site to explore your own numbers.

For more detailed award rates, visit the [pay guides](/blog) page. To compare your pay with averages, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) section.
